questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, how can a driver slow down?

options.text: Let the truck run out of gas.

questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear helps slow your vehicle down if hydraulic brakes fail.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Increase the space in front of your vehicle to make it easier for the tailgater to pass. Speeding up is dangerous because the other driver may continue tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hope the vehicle lasts until someone else drives it.
Stop and inspect the vehicle to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and inspect the vehicle to find the problem.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, stop and inspect the source right away.

questions.question: Which tire condition is acceptable?

options.text: Dual tires that do not touch each other
Mismatched tire sizes on short trips
Retreaded tires on the front of a school bus

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual tires that do not touch each other
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or other vehicle parts. Tire sizes must match. Retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus. Tires must not be cut or damaged.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, what must you do?
questions.explanation: When exiting, face the vehicle and keep contact with the handrail at all times. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To keep the cargo a secret

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep the cargo a secret
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people from spills and to protect cargo from weather. Keeping cargo secret is not a reason to cover it.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/right parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: Pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.
Estimate the weight of cargo in a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the CDL vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
The total weight of the vehicle without a load
The total weight of cargo minus the containers
The maximum weight allowed to be transported by a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: GVWR is the loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What happens when driving in extremely hot weather?

options.text: You need to remove oil from the engine.

questions.explanation: In extremely hot weather, tire pressure can increase to dangerous levels as air expands in heat. Keep enough oil and coolant in the engine to prevent overheating.

questions.question: Is driving at night safer or more dangerous?

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. Drivers cannot see as well. Headlight glare affects vision. There are more tired and drunk drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It usually happens at speeds above 65 mph.
It can happen with just a little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip and slide on water. You do not need a lot of water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. Are these tar spots slippery?

options.text: No, they grip the road like normal.
No, they grip better than the rest of the road.
Yes, they will stop your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch for tar spots on the road in very hot weather. These areas are very slippery.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air?

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if pressure gets too high. If it starts releasing air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic check and fix the problem.

questions.question: What is one way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your tires have good tread.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, hydroplaning risk increases if your tires are under-inflated or worn. If you start to hydroplane, release the gas and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: When you pull over on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: Always turn on your emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This warns other drivers. It is especially important at night.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, use one second of distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: How should exhaust system parts be?
questions.explanation: Check that exhaust system parts are not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be mounted properly and should not rub against moving parts.

questions.question: What should you do with manual air tank drains?

options.text: Open them at the end of each day to drain the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open them at the end of each day to drain the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open manual drains daily to remove water and oil.

questions.question: When does a bridge freeze compared to other road surfaces?

options.text: Only when temperature drops well below 32 degrees.
Bridges have heaters to prevent freezing.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular road surfaces. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: If a vehicle has a vehicle inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Not look at the report and find any issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.explanation: Review the last inspection report for your vehicle. The carrier should have fixed any problems listed in the report.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly to:

options.text: Follow the rule to always accelerate slowly.
Not go faster than the vehicle ahead.
Be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.explanation: Speeding up too fast on slippery roads can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air brake system within:
questions.explanation: In a single air brake system, the air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within three minutes after the engine is running at normal speed.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, the driver should:
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brake pedal so the wheels can roll again. Then steer in the direction you want to go, and steer back the other way to prevent skidding in the opposite direction.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Not worry about how the weight is spread.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance the cargo weight evenly in the trailer. Too much or too little weight on an axle makes the vehicle hard to control. Too much weight on one axle can also damage it.

questions.question: If a law enforcement officer asks you to take a blood alcohol test:

options.text: You can refuse without any penalty.
You can refuse but will pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have an Implied Consent Law. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if a police officer asks. If you refuse, you will lose your license. Know the laws in every state where you drive.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks down:

options.text: A yellow light will turn on in the instrument panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light will turn on in the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: When ABS breaks down, a yellow warning light on the instrument panel will alert you that the braking system is not working properly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, a CDL applicant may be asked to:
questions.explanation: The CDL vehicle inspection test includes checking the engine oil level as part of a full vehicle inspection.

questions.question: An applicant will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if they:
questions.explanation: Your hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you do not have legal permanent status in the U.S., renounce U.S. citizenship, are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, are judged mentally incompetent, or are considered a security risk by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: When you complete a written vehicle inspection report, you must sign it:

options.text: Only when defects are noted and repairs are certified as completed.
Only when repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a law enforcement officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when defects are noted and repairs are certified as completed.
questions.explanation: You must sign the inspection report only if defects were found and repairs have been certified as completed or not needed.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels and located on the vehicle's axles. The braking parts that stop the vehicle are found inside the brake drum.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Are safe if you only drive on highways.

questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps the vehicle's axles in place. Damaged suspension parts like leaking shock absorbers are serious safety defects.

questions.question: When driving, knowing what is happening behind you is:
questions.explanation: Safe driving means you must know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Use your mirrors often to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends mainly on how much alcohol you drank, how fast you drank it, and your body weight.

questions.question: You can avoid distracted driving by:

options.text: Setting radio stations before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Setting radio stations before you drive.
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical (reaching for objects), mental (talking with passengers), or both (using a phone). To avoid distracted driving: set radio stations ahead of time, plan your route before leaving, avoid serious conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while behind the wheel.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest speed to drive is:

options.text: Slower than the traffic around you.
The same speed as the traffic around you.
Faster than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles go the same direction at the same speed, they cannot crash into each other.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch and:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, the brake lights turn on when you press the brake pedal and air pressure moves an electric switch.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from rolling.
Use wheel chocks only after you apply the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from rolling.
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, use wheel chocks. If your vehicle does not have spring brakes, this is essential to prevent it from rolling.

questions.question: In cold temperatures, when do bridges usually freeze?

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Drive with extra caution on bridges and overpasses when roads are wet and temperatures are low.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: When brakes overheat, they can fail. The heat causes chemical changes that make brakes less effective. This is called brake fade. Eventually, the brakes may stop working completely.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should be your main way to control speed?
questions.explanation: Use engine braking as your main way to control speed on steep hills. Downshift before going down. Using only the brakes can cause them to overheat and fail.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean they are loose. Check that wheel nuts are tight before you drive.

questions.question: What happens after two violations of state hand-held phone laws?

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service.
You must drive 10 mph under the speed limit for a period of time.

questions.explanation: Two violations of hand-held phone use laws will result in CDL disqualification. Future violations have even more serious consequences.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what should you expect?

options.text: It will probably stay green as you approach.
It will likely change to yellow soon.
It will skip yellow and change directly from green to red.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will likely change to yellow soon.
questions.explanation: When a green light has been on for a long time, it will probably turn yellow soon. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?

options.text: It is required on slippery surfaces.

questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and other parts.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes at an intersection, which should you use?

options.text: It doesn't matter which lane you use.

questions.explanation: When there are two left turn lanes, use the rightmost lane to make your left turn safely.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: Where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water sits on the road. Low tire pressure or worn tires increase the risk. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic.
When vehicles are too close to one another.

questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a driver turns or changes lanes too quickly.
